title: Add nightly mixed-workload scheduler canary job (short/long prompts) + regression alerts
author: Sahana Iyer
release_notes: Adds a nightly canary job that runs standardized mixed short/long prompt workloads against runtime candidates and posts regression alerts (p95/TTFT/throughput) to #eng-runtime and #eng-sre.
body: Summary: Introduces a new scheduled canary job for the mixed-workload scheduler prototype (short/long prompt-aware policy) to catch tail latency regressions before we ramp the feature flag in prod. The job runs nightly on a small set of representative SKUs/regions and publishes results + alerting based on agreed thresholds. Context: Runtime scheduler work (two-queue + aging, prefill/decode separation) has shown improvements on mixed distributions, but we saw at least one canary p95 spike during early ramp; this adds automated coverage so we fail fast on parameter changes or kernel selection instability. Linked to ENG-2456. What’s included: 1) New job definition: nightly schedule (cron), matrix of targets (regions + GPU SKU), runtime version selection (latest candidate tag). 2) Mixed workload scenarios: imports standard mixes (80/20 short/long, 50/50, long-spike) and runs with fixed seeds for repeatability; includes a short warmup phase and consistent run protocol. 3) Result parsing + baselining: writes a compact JSON artifact per scenario with p50/p95/p99, TTFT, throughput (tok/s), and queue-time; compares against the last successful run on the same target and flags deltas. 4) Alerting: posts a summary to Slack with a per-scenario table, links to artifacts, and a “regression” section listing any threshold violations; routes to #eng-runtime and #eng-sre. 5) Guardrails: skips alerting on infra-level failures (capacity/timeout) but still posts a “job unhealthy” message with retry guidance; adds explicit timeouts so the job can’t hang and block the canary queue. Metrics + thresholds (initial): - p95 end-to-end latency regression: > +10% (hard fail) - TTFT regression: > +15% (warn), > +25% (fail) - throughput regression: < -7% (fail) - job health: missing artifacts, scenario timeout, or runner crash triggers “unhealthy” (warn) These align with the draft rollout guardrails we’ve been using in ENG-2470; we can tune once we have a week of data. Notes: - This PR intentionally does not encode scheduler policy knobs; it uses the runtime under test default config and only sets workload mix parameters. The goal is to catch changes caused by runtime candidates, kernel selection, or accidental policy default drift. - Regions/SKUs are deliberately small to control GPU spend; see “Target matrix” below. Target matrix (v1): - us-east-1 / A100-80G - us-west-2 / H100 - eu-west-1 / L40S (best-effort runner capacity) Follow-ups (out of scope here): - Add a weekly “trace replay lite” job once the anonymized trace pack is stable (tracked in ENG-2449). - Add a dedicated dashboard panel to aggregate canary deltas over time (Allison has a spec draft).
commits: Add mixed-workload nightly job scaffold + schedule
Add scenario config for 80/20, 50/50, and long-spike mixes
Implement result parser + baseline comparison (last successful run)
Slack notifier: regression summary + links to artifacts
Harden runner timeouts + infra failure classification
Docs: add runbook snippet for interpreting mixed-workload canary
review_conversation: Allison Grant: Can we standardize the Slack message fields to match other perf-canary alerts (title prefix, target label formatting, and include links to artifacts + run logs)? Also please include a single-line SRE-friendly rollback hint when we see a hard fail. Sahana Iyer (author): Updated Slack payload to match existing notifier helpers; added artifact/run-log links and a “Suggested action” line for hard fails. Aisha Bello: Thresholds look aggressive for TTFT on long-spike. Can we make TTFT fail threshold higher until we have baseline variance? Also I’d like infra failures to page less; post to channel but don’t mark as regression. Sahana Iyer (author): Adjusted TTFT thresholds (warn 15%, fail 25%) and split infra failure classification from performance regressions; infra failures now post “job unhealthy” without regression tagging. Lena Fischer: For the runtime candidate selection—are we pinned to a tag or “latest”? We need deterministic comparisons if the candidate changes during the run window. Sahana Iyer (author): Pinned the job to resolve the candidate tag at start of run and write it into the artifact; baseline comparisons are keyed by (target, scenario, resolved_candidate_tag). Claire Dubois: Please add an option to override seeds so we can reproduce locally, and ensure the warmup is excluded from reported latencies. Sahana Iyer (author): Added seed override and confirmed warmup is excluded from the measured window; updated docs accordingly. Rina Kobayashi: Looks good; small request—rename scenario identifiers to match benchmark-lab naming (mixed_80_20, mixed_50_50, mixed_long_spike). Sahana Iyer (author): Renamed identifiers + updated parser and Slack formatter. Rina Kobayashi: Approved. Allison Grant: Approved. Aisha Bello: Approved after thresholds change.
merge_outcome: Merged into main; nightly schedule enabled for us-east-1 and us-west-2 immediately, eu-west-1 marked best-effort pending runner capacity.
